eu-battery-durability-80-72.licence_note: European Parliament press release; reproduction authorised with the source acknowledged. Restated in our own words.

hybrid-mild-vs-full-savings.fact: fueleconomy.gov estimates of efficiency gains: a stop-start system alone about 2%, a mild hybrid 3-6%, and a full hybrid 27-35%.
hybrid-mild-vs-full-savings.licence_note: US federal government work (fueleconomy.gov, DOE/EPA), public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Restated in our own words.

turbo-small-engine-why.fact: fueleconomy.gov: turbochargers increase engine power, which lets manufacturers use smaller engines without losing performance; with that downsizing, turbocharging can raise efficiency by up to 8%.
turbo-small-engine-why.licence_note: US federal government work (fueleconomy.gov, DOE/EPA), public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Restated in our own words.

hybrid-how-it-saves.fact: fueleconomy.gov: a hybrid saves fuel because regenerative braking recaptures energy normally lost when coasting or braking; the electric motor assists the engine when accelerating, passing or climbing, so a smaller, more efficient engine can be used; in some hybrids the motor alone propels the car at low speeds, where petrol engines are least efficient; and the engine shuts off automatically when the car stops and restarts when the accelerator is pressed.
hybrid-how-it-saves.licence_note: US federal government work (fueleconomy.gov, DOE/EPA), public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Restated in our own words.

hybrid-brake-gently-early.fact: Toyota UK: in a hybrid, braking gently and early lets the regenerative braking recover more energy, so the car can run in EV mode for longer.
hybrid-brake-gently-early.licence_note: Toyota UK magazine (manufacturer) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

hybrid-b-mode-descents.fact: Toyota UK: the B position on a Toyota hybrid's gear selector gives engine braking, useful when descending a steep hill; it is not recommended for normal driving because it uses more fuel.
hybrid-b-mode-descents.licence_note: Toyota UK magazine (manufacturer) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

hybrid-two-batteries-12v.fact: Toyota UK: a hybrid has an ordinary 12 V battery as well as the hybrid battery, and the two do different jobs; a discharged 12 V battery can stop smart entry and other electrical systems from working normally.
hybrid-two-batteries-12v.licence_note: Toyota UK magazine (manufacturer) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

hybrid-standing-ready-mode.fact: Toyota UK (advice from 2020 for cars standing unused): to keep both batteries of a Toyota hybrid charged, put it in READY mode (in Park, parking brake on) for about 60 minutes and repeat at least once a week; Toyota says a drive is not needed. Never leave the car unattended in READY, and do this only in a well-ventilated place, which matters if the car is kept in a garage.
hybrid-standing-ready-mode.licence_note: Toyota UK magazine (manufacturer) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

ev-regen-city-vs-motorway.fact: ADAC tests (March 2024): electric cars recover on average about 30% of their energy through regenerative braking in city traffic (the Nio and Hyundai Ioniq 6 over 40%), but only about 10% on the motorway.
ev-regen-city-vs-motorway.licence_note: ADAC (German automobile club) press release, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

ev-brake-discs-rust.fact: ADAC: because an electric car does most of its slowing by regenerative braking, the mechanical brakes are used less and the discs can rust; ADAC advises braking harder now and then to clean them, but only when traffic allows it safely.
ev-brake-discs-rust.licence_note: ADAC (German automobile club) press release, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

ev-hybrid-warning-sound-30kmh.fact: US safety standard FMVSS 141: electric and hybrid cars must emit a sound so pedestrians can detect them when moving forward below 30 km/h, when stationary with the propulsion system active in a forward gear or neutral, and when reversing.
ev-hybrid-warning-sound-30kmh.licence_note: US federal regulation (49 CFR 571.141), a US government work in the public domain, read on Cornell LII's copy. Restated in our own words.

tpms-light-flashing-fault.fact: US standard FMVSS 138: where one tyre-pressure light also shows system faults, a light that flashes for 60 to 90 seconds each time the car is started and then stays lit means the monitoring system itself has a fault; a light that simply stays on means a tyre is significantly underinflated. The owner's manual must also state that the system is not a substitute for proper tyre maintenance.
tpms-light-flashing-fault.licence_note: US federal regulation (49 CFR 571.138), a US government work in the public domain, read on Cornell LII's copy. Restated in our own words.

keyless-relay-half-open.fact: ADAC (18 August 2026): over ten years it has tested more than 850 cars with keyless entry by extending the key's radio signal; almost half can still be opened this way, and in about one case in three the engine could be started too. Manufacturers that improved their systems mostly use ultra-wideband (UWB), which ADAC says counts as well secured by the current state of technology.
keyless-relay-half-open.licence_note: ADAC (German automobile club) press release, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

keyless-relay-protect.fact: ADAC: relay thieves use two small devices, one near the key and one at the car door, stretching the signal over hundreds of metres. ADAC's advice: switch keyless off if the owner's manual allows it, at home keep the key away from outer doors, walls and windows, and if you use a metal tin or shielding pouch, test that it really blocks every signal.
keyless-relay-protect.licence_note: ADAC (German automobile club) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

key-fob-dead-battery-start.fact: Mazda CX-5 owner's manual: with a dead key battery the engine can still be started: keep the brake pedal firmly pressed, hold the centre of the emblem on the key against the start button while its green light flashes, then press the button. Each car's backup method is in its own manual.
key-fob-dead-battery-start.licence_note: Mazda owner's manual page (manufacturer), copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

smart-key-hidden-metal-key.fact: Toyota UK: most Toyota smart keys contain a mechanical emergency key for when the electrical systems are unavailable, and the driver's door has a concealed key cylinder, usually behind a small panel on the door handle.
smart-key-hidden-metal-key.licence_note: Toyota UK magazine (manufacturer) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

adas-windscreen-camera-recalibration.fact: AAA: camera sensors for systems such as automatic emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, lane departure warning and lane keeping usually sit behind the windscreen, often with the rear-view mirror. Windscreen replacement is one of the jobs that can call for recalibration; a sensor off by just one degree is aimed significantly off target 50 or more feet (about 15 m) down the road; and many automakers specify only original (OEM) glass for camera-equipped cars.
adas-windscreen-camera-recalibration.licence_note: AAA page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

adas-radar-blocked-snow.fact: Kia owner's manual: when dirt, snow or debris covers the front radar cover, Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist may stop working temporarily and the display reports the radar is blocked; clean the cover. Kia also says not to fit plate mouldings, bumper stickers or bumper guards near the radar, and never to put stickers or tint on the windscreen.
adas-radar-blocked-snow.licence_note: Kia owner's manual page (manufacturer), copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

adas-bumper-knock-radar.fact: Kia owner's manual: if the front radar or camera is forced out of alignment, for example by damage to the front bumper near the radar, Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist may not work correctly, and a warning message may not be displayed; have it checked by a workshop.
adas-bumper-knock-radar.licence_note: Kia owner's manual page (manufacturer), copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

adas-pedestrian-braking-night.fact: AAA tests: in 2019 the pedestrian automatic emergency braking systems tested avoided none of the night-time collisions with an adult crossing the road; in 2025 tests of four 2024-2025 cars at 40 km/h, night-time avoidance reached 60%. At night, high-visibility clothing ranged from helping to a complete loss of detection.
adas-pedestrian-braking-night.licence_note: AAA newsroom page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

aeb-halves-rear-end-crashes.fact: IIHS: forward collision warning combined with automatic emergency braking cuts rear-end crashes in half, while the warning alone cuts them by 27%; blind-spot detection reduces lane-change crashes by 14%.
aeb-halves-rear-end-crashes.licence_note: IIHS page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

led-headlights-no-guarantee.fact: IIHS: headlights are rated on the same performance test whatever their light source; using LEDs does not guarantee a good rating, and poor ratings exist for every type of headlamp.
led-headlights-no-guarantee.licence_note: IIHS page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

matrix-headlights-shade-others.fact: IIHS: adaptive driving beam ('matrix') headlights keep the high beam on but continuously reshape it to put a shadow around other vehicles; in a 2015 IIHS study their glare was significantly lower than that of an SUV with HID low beams. They had been available in Europe for over a decade before a 2022 US rule change allowed them there.
matrix-headlights-shade-others.licence_note: IIHS page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

high-beams-underused.fact: IIHS: in one study only 18% of drivers who were isolated enough to use high beams did so; in an IIHS test a 2024 Subaru Solterra driver could spot an obstacle 202 ft (about 62 m) ahead on low beams but 533 ft (about 162 m) on high beams. High-beam assist uses a camera to switch between the two automatically.
high-beams-underused.licence_note: IIHS page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

led-bulb-halogen-mot-fail.fact: UK MOT inspection manual: on vehicles first used on or after 1 April 1986, existing halogen headlamp units must not be converted to take HID or LED bulbs, and a converted headlamp fails the test; a complete replacement headlamp unit made with HID or LED light sources is not failed for that reason if it meets the other requirements.
led-bulb-halogen-mot-fail.licence_note: GOV.UK, Crown copyright, Open Government Licence v3.0 (free reuse with attribution: 'Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0'). Restated in our own words.

obd-port-key-programming-theft.fact: Toyota UK: every new car sold in the UK since 2003 has an on-board diagnostic (OBD) port, and thieves have found that with special equipment they can use it to program blank keys; some owners fit an aftermarket OBD lock, either a lockable metal box over the port or an electronic lock that works with the immobiliser.
obd-port-key-programming-theft.licence_note: Toyota UK magazine (manufacturer) page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

eu-isa-speed-warning.fact: EU: Intelligent Speed Assistance became mandatory on new car models in July 2022 and on all new cars sold in July 2024; it warns the driver when over the speed limit by a sound, a vibration, feedback through the accelerator pedal or gently reducing speed, but the driver is always in control and can override it by pressing the accelerator.
eu-isa-speed-warning.licence_note: © European Union (European Road Safety Charter, European Commission); reuse authorised with acknowledgement under the Commission's reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU). Restated in our own words.

edr-crash-black-box.fact: US rule 49 CFR Part 563: a light vehicle fitted with an event data recorder must store, for the 5 seconds before a crash, the indicated speed, the accelerator position and whether the service brake was pressed (2 samples per second), plus whether the driver's seat belt was fastened. An updated rule raises the pre-crash window to 20 seconds at 10 samples per second, phased in from September 2028 and applying to vehicles built from 1 September 2031 (small-volume and multi-stage manufacturers later).
edr-crash-black-box.licence_note: US federal regulation (49 CFR 563.7), a US government work in the public domain, read on Cornell LII's copy. Restated in our own words.

phev-real-world-3-5x.fact: European Commission (March 2024): plug-in hybrids registered in 2021 emitted on average 3.5 times more CO2 on the road than their official figures (about 4 l/100 km more fuel), mainly because they are not charged and driven electrically as often as assumed.
phev-real-world-3-5x.licence_note: © European Union (DG Climate Action); reuse authorised with acknowledgement under the Commission's reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU). Restated in our own words.

real-fuel-use-vs-official.fact: European Commission (March 2024): since January 2021 every new EU car running on liquid fuel must carry an on-board fuel consumption meter; its data showed real-world CO2 emissions (which track fuel use) 23.7% above the official figures for petrol cars and 18.1% for diesel cars (2021 data).
real-fuel-use-vs-official.licence_note: © European Union (DG Climate Action); reuse authorised with acknowledgement under the Commission's reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU). Restated in our own words.

dct-hill-hold-brake.fact: Kia owner's manual (dual-clutch transmission): holding the car on a hill with the accelerator, or creeping without the brake, can overheat and damage the clutch and transmission; hold it with the foot brake or parking brake, and in uphill stop-and-go traffic leave some distance ahead before moving forward, then hold the car with the foot brake.
dct-hill-hold-brake.licence_note: Kia owner's manual page (manufacturer), copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

start-stop-conditions.fact: Mazda CX-90 owner's manual (2026; this model is a mild hybrid): i-stop stops the engine only when conditions are met, among them a fully warmed-up engine, transmission fluid warm but not abnormally hot, the battery's (on this model the M Hybrid Boost battery's) charge and temperature being good, the cabin temperature close to the A/C setting, the steering wheel nearly straight, the car not on a steep slope and the bonnet closed. It may not operate right after the lead-acid (12 V) battery terminals are reconnected, and after a battery replacement the system should be checked.
start-stop-conditions.licence_note: Mazda owner's manual page (manufacturer), copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

gdi-intake-valve-carbon.fact: SAE technical paper 2016-01-2252: petrol direct-injection engines tend to form intake valve deposits because the fuel no longer washes the valves as in port-injected engines; the deposits come from a combination of engine oil, engine-wear elements, unburned fuel and exhaust contaminants, can cause poorer combustion, unstable running, valve sticking or engine failure, often have to be removed by expensive mechanical cleaning, and build up at a rate affected by the engine oil's formulation.
gdi-intake-valve-carbon.licence_note: SAE International technical paper abstract, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

api-sp-oil-turbo.fact: API: the API SP petrol engine-oil category, introduced in May 2020, was designed to protect against low-speed pre-ignition (LSPI) and timing-chain wear and to improve high-temperature deposit protection for pistons and turbochargers. A newer category, API SQ, may be shown on oils from 31 March 2025 (API 1509, 23rd edition). For petrol engines, the latest API category includes the performance of every earlier one.
api-sp-oil-turbo.licence_note: American Petroleum Institute page, copyrighted: only the facts are used, restated in our own words, no text copied.

ge-gap-2s-3s-law.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 25(10)(პ): in normal traffic the time needed to close the gap to the vehicle in front must be at least 2 seconds in a built-up area and at least 3 seconds outside built-up areas (this does not apply when pulling out to overtake after signalling).
ge-gap-2s-3s-law.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-gap-ice-6s-9s.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 25(10)(ჟ): on an icy road the following gap must take at least 6 seconds to cover in a built-up area and at least 9 seconds outside built-up areas.
ge-gap-ice-6s-9s.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-dip-beam-150m.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 49(2)(ბ): main beam must be switched to dipped beam at least 150 m before meeting an oncoming vehicle, and earlier if the oncoming driver signals the need by flashing their headlights.
ge-dip-beam-150m.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-daytime-headlights-when.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 49(1),(7)-(8), Art. 42 and Art. 5(7): at night and whenever visibility is insufficient (under 300 m because of fog, rain, snow and the like, or in a tunnel), every moving motor vehicle must have dipped or main beam and rear position lamps on. In good daylight, dipped headlights and rear position lamps are compulsory only in listed cases: in an organised convoy, when carrying a group of children by bus or suitably equipped truck, for oversize, overweight or dangerous-goods vehicles, on the towing vehicle when towing, and for route vehicles in a contra-flow bus lane; every motorcycle must show at least one dipped headlight in front by day, and headlights must be on in a tunnel marked by a sign.
ge-daytime-headlights-when.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-horn-only-to-warn.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 48: the horn may be used only to warn other road users in time to avoid a crash, or outside built-up areas to warn a driver that you intend to overtake; it must not sound longer than needed, and neither the horn nor flashing headlights gives the driver priority. Breaking the horn rules falls under the 50 GEL fine of the Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(6).
ge-horn-only-to-warn.licence_note: Official legal acts of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated versions read 2026-10-12; the fine is in the Administrative Offences Code, https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/28216. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-tow-rope-4-6m.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 45(5),(9) and Art. 38(4): when towing on a flexible link the gap between the two vehicles must be 4 to 6 m, on a rigid tow bar no more than 4 m; a flexible link must carry at least two flags or warning devices (or a 200x200 mm board with 50 mm red and white reflective diagonal stripes); a vehicle towed with a home-made link such as a rope or wire may not enter a motorway.
ge-tow-rope-4-6m.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-tow-50kmh-no-rope-on-ice.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 33(8)(დ) and Art. 45(6)(ე),(7): a vehicle towing another may go no faster than 50 km/h; at any time of day the towing vehicle must have its dipped headlights on and the towed vehicle its hazard lights (or a warning triangle on its rear if it has none); towing on a flexible link is banned when the road is icy.
ge-tow-50kmh-no-rope-on-ice.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-tow-no-brakes-half-mass.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 45(6)(გ): a vehicle whose braking system does not work may not be towed if its actual mass is more than half the towing vehicle's actual mass; if it is lighter than that, it may be towed only on a rigid bar or partly lifted onto the towing vehicle, not on a rope.
ge-tow-no-brakes-half-mass.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-warning-triangle-15-30m.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 52(2),(3),(5): after switching on the hazard lights at a crash, or at a forced stop where stopping is banned or others cannot see the car in time, the driver must at once set out the warning triangle (a flashing red lamp in poor visibility) at a distance that warns others in time but no less than 15 m from the vehicle in a built-up area and 30 m outside; the triangle's sides must be at least 0.4 m with a red border at least 0.05 m wide.
ge-warning-triangle-15-30m.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-livestock-driver-not-liable.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 22(9): if an animal that was on the road unattended, or there in breach of the grazing or herding rules, is killed or injured in a road crash, the driver is released from the duty to compensate for that harm.
ge-livestock-driver-not-liable.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-livestock-herder-rules.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 22(1),(6),(8): animals on the road must have a herder in constant control, and herding on the road is allowed from age 16; herders may not leave animals on the road unattended, may not drive livestock along asphalt or concrete roads where another road exists, and should as a rule move animals across roads in daylight. (Administrative Offences Code Art. 127(2): breaking these rules on international or national roads costs the herder, or failing that the owner, 10 GEL.)
ge-livestock-herder-rules.licence_note: Official legal acts of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated versions read 2026-10-12; the fine is in the Administrative Offences Code, https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/28216. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright; restated in our own words.

ge-no-car-wash-in-river.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 16(2): washing a vehicle in the sea, a lake, a reservoir, a river or any other surface water body, or on their banks closer than 10 m to the water, is not allowed.
ge-no-car-wash-in-river.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-yard-no-idling.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 44: in a signed residential zone pedestrians may use the full width of the road and children may play, drivers may go no faster than 20 km/h, and through traffic, learner driving and standing with the engine running are banned; the article's rules also apply in courtyards (ezo).
ge-yard-no-idling.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-child-under-6-alone.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 26(9): it is forbidden to leave a child under 6 unattended in a stopped vehicle.
ge-child-under-6-alone.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-passengers-kerb-side.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 23 and Art. 46(8): passengers get in and out only after the vehicle has fully stopped, from the pavement or verge side (from the roadway side only if that is impossible and does not obstruct others), and must not open the door of a moving vehicle; the driver may move off only with the doors closed and must not open them before a full stop.
ge-passengers-kerb-side.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-blind-pedestrian-priority.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 21(6): a driver must in every case give way to a blind pedestrian walking with a white cane or a guide dog.
ge-blind-pedestrian-priority.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-no-stop-5m-crossing.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 37(6)(ა): stopping on the carriageway is banned on pedestrian and cycle crossings and within 5 m before them, and on an intersection or within 5 m of its edges (with a narrow exception at certain T-junctions with a solid line or dividing strip).
ge-no-stop-5m-crossing.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-fine-parking-by-city.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(8),(8¹)-(8³): breaking a no-stopping or no-parking sign or another stopping or parking rule costs 10 GEL, but 50 GEL in Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi, Mtskheta, Rustavi, Gori, Telavi, Poti, Zugdidi, Akhaltsikhe, Ozurgeti or any resort; stopping or parking on a pavement or pedestrian crossing (where not allowed) costs 10 GEL, or 100 GEL in those cities and resorts; parking without the right in a disabled bay or blocking a ramp costs 200 GEL, and ignoring a no-stopping-at-fire-hydrant sign 200 GEL.
ge-fine-parking-by-city.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-pavement-bus-lane.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(6⁶),(12)-(13): driving on a pavement costs 200 GEL; driving, stopping or parking in a with-flow bus lane 100 GEL (150 GEL if repeated within a year) and in a contra-flow bus lane 200 GEL (300 GEL if repeated); driving, stopping or parking in a cycle lane or on a cycle path 100 GEL.
ge-fine-pavement-bus-lane.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-solid-line.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(7¹)-(7³) and note 9: crossing the solid centre line separating opposite flows costs 50 GEL (100 GEL if repeated within a year); crossing it and driving against the flow costs 200 GEL, which applies when the car fully crosses the line.
ge-fine-solid-line.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-speeding-tiers.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(1)-(1²),(4),(5): exceeding the speed limit by more than 15 km/h but no more than 30 km/h costs 50 GEL, by more than 30 up to 50 km/h 100 GEL, and by more than 50 km/h 300 GEL; if the speeding creates an emergency situation the fine is 400 GEL, and 600 GEL if it causes light damage or light injury. The limit itself is binding in full (Law on Road Traffic, Art. 33).
ge-fine-speeding-tiers.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-average-speed-cameras.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125, note 10: speeding also counts when automatic cameras installed on a road section calculate, from the distance between them and the time taken, that the driver went faster than the limit over that stretch.
ge-average-speed-cameras.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-licence-points-100.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 58(2²)-(2⁶): every Georgian-issued driving licence is credited with 100 points on 1 January each year; leftover points are cancelled and reset to 100 the next 1 January; traffic offences take points off, and reaching zero suspends the right to drive every category for 1 year; the Interior Ministry warns the holder by email or SMS when the points fall to 50 and again to 20, if it has their contact details. (A foreign licence is credited 100 points once, Art. 58(2⁷).)
ge-licence-points-100.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-camera-fines-no-points.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 58(2⁹): administrative offences recorded on photo or video do not reduce the points credited to a driving licence.
ge-camera-fines-no-points.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-fine-late-surcharge.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 290(1),(1¹), Art. 290¹(3),(4) and Art. 125 notes 3, 5, 6: a traffic fine under Art. 125 must be paid within 30 days; after that a surcharge of double the fine, capped at 500 GEL, is added and there are another 30 days to pay both. For a ticket written by police on the spot, if it is still unpaid the right to drive is suspended for 6 months, and neither paying nor the suspension cancels the surcharge. For a fine recorded on camera, the same surcharge applies, but if fine and surcharge are still unpaid 30 days later the vehicle is sold to cover them (if the person charged owns it).
ge-fine-late-surcharge.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Municipal parking fines follow a different surcharge rule (Art. 125 note 4²).

ge-fine-seatbelt-driver-pays.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 118¹: if the driver, or the passenger sitting next to the driver, does not wear a seat belt while the vehicle is moving, the driver is fined 50 GEL.
ge-fine-seatbelt-driver-pays.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-drink-drive-limits.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 116(1),(2),(10): drunk driving means more than 0.3 per mille of alcohol in the blood; from over 0.3 up to 0.7 per mille the right to drive is suspended for 6 months, and above 0.7 per mille, or for avoiding the test, for 1 year.
ge-drink-drive-limits.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Penalties change: recheck before each film.

ge-alcohol-falls-015-per-hour.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 116, note 10: when a blood test is assessed, the deciding body works from the figure, based on studies of how the body processes alcohol, that the alcohol concentration in the body falls by 0.15 per mille every hour.
ge-alcohol-falls-015-per-hour.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. The figure is the law's own, not medical advice.

ge-tint-side-windows.fact: Georgia, Interior Minister's Order No. 165 of 28 February 2014 as amended by Order No. 47 of 2 July 2024: without Patrol Police consent, tinting may reduce the light transmission of the front side windows by no more than 60% and of the side windows beside the passengers behind the driver by no more than 75%; consent for darker windows is given mainly to government members, state-protected officials and special services (Order 165, Art. 4(2), or in exceptional cases Art. 4(8)).
ge-tint-side-windows.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), the amending order read 2026-10-12 (later amendments of 2025 did not change these percentages). Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-tint-windshield-factory.fact: Georgia, Interior Minister's Order No. 14 of 26 March 2024 amending Order No. 165: reducing the light transmission of the windshield is banned, except a tint applied by the vehicle's manufacturer that reduces it by no more than 30%.
ge-tint-windshield-factory.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), read 2026-10-12. Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-fine-tint.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 119(7),(7¹),(7²) and note 9: windows tinted beyond the Interior Minister's norm by no more than 10% cost 100 GEL, beyond it by more than 10% cost 500 GEL, and a repeat within 1 year costs 1,000 GEL; with the fine the driver gets 3 days to fix it, during which no further fine for it is given.
ge-fine-tint.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-visible-smoke.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 119²: driving a vehicle with visible exhaust that breaks the legal emission norm in Tbilisi, Batumi, Kutaisi or Rustavi, or dodging the check, costs the driver 100 GEL; repeating it after 15 days costs 300 GEL, then 600 GEL; the driver is freed from the fine if within 2 hours an accredited inspection centre, at the driver's cost, finds the exhaust within the norm.
ge-fine-visible-smoke.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-noise.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 119(3⁴)-(3⁶): driving a vehicle whose operating noise exceeds the norm set by government resolution costs 100 GEL, 200 GEL the second time and 300 GEL after that.
ge-fine-noise.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-homemade-mods.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 119(5) and note 9¹: driving a vehicle modified on the owner's own initiative (altered fuel tank, body or silencer, a fitted natural-gas system, or other design changes) that does not meet road-safety requirements or the manufacturer's standards costs 200 GEL; police may take the driver off the wheel and send the car to an impound lot, from which it is returned only after 10 days, the offender paying transport and storage.
ge-fine-homemade-mods.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-wiper-broken-ban.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 21(13), with Administrative Offences Code Art. 119(2): it is banned to drive with a faulty service brake, steering or trailer coupling, at night on an unlit road with both headlights or the rear position lamps out, or in fog, rain or snow when the wiper on the driver's side does not work; driving with faulty brakes, steering or coupling, with the headlights or rear lamps out at night, with a dead wiper in rain or snow, or with a leaking engine fuel system costs 50 GEL.
ge-wiper-broken-ban.licence_note: Official legal acts of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated versions read 2026-10-12; the fine is in the Administrative Offences Code, https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/28216. Official texts are not protected by copyright; restated in our own words.

ge-fine-winter-tyres.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 119(2¹) and notes 17-18: driving on a listed road section in the legal winter period without proper winter tyres on every wheel, or without anti-skid chains when they are required, costs 100 GEL; the police may stop the vehicle going on, and it may be taken to an impound lot until the case is decided, the offender paying transport and storage. The legal winter period is 1 December to 1 March (Government Resolution No. 526, as in ge-winter-tyre-period).
ge-fine-winter-tyres.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Replaces the dropped 'ge-winter-fine', which rested only on a news report.

ge-winter-tbilisi-bypass.fact: Georgia, Government Resolution No. 526 (in force 1 January 2024), annex 2: the winter-tyre list includes the whole Tbilisi bypass road (S-9), 49 km from Zahesi to Rustavi, so from 1 December to 1 March every wheel needs proper winter tyres there.
ge-winter-tbilisi-bypass.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), read 2026-10-12. Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-winter-resort-roads.fact: Georgia, Government Resolution No. 526, annex 2: the winter-tyre sections include the Batumi (Angisa) to Akhaltsikhe road from Keda to Akhaltsikhe (138 km), the whole Chokhatauri to Bakhmaro road (53 km), the Bakuriani ring road, the access road to the Didveli ski complex, and the Vaziani to Gombori to Telavi road from Sasadilo to Telavi.
ge-winter-resort-roads.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), read 2026-10-12. Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-winter-total-km.fact: Georgia, Government Resolution No. 526, annex 2: the roads where winter tyres are compulsory from 1 December to 1 March total 369.5 km of international roads and 1,309.9 km of domestic roads, about 1,679 km in all.
ge-winter-total-km.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), read 2026-10-12. Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; the sum is our own arithmetic from the act's two totals.

ge-unknown-surface-secondary.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 36(6),(8): if a driver cannot tell whether their road has a surface (because of darkness, snow, mud or anything else) and there are no priority signs, they are treated as being on the secondary road; and unless a sign says otherwise, a driver coming off a dirt road onto a road that is not dirt must give way to traffic on it.
ge-unknown-surface-secondary.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-blocked-junction.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 36(5) and Art. 25(6): a driver must not enter an intersection if a jam means they will probably have to stop on it and block crossing traffic, even when the lights allow them to go; likewise a driver must not enter a pedestrian crossing without being sure they will not have to stop on it.
ge-blocked-junction.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-yellow-light-means-stop.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 29(2)(გ),(ვ),(14): a steady yellow light forbids moving on and warns that the signal is about to change; a driver who cannot stop at the stop line without braking hard may continue; a flashing green means the green phase is about to end.
ge-yellow-light-means-stop.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-green-arrow-u-turn.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 29(10): an arrow on a traffic light means the same as a full light of that colour but only for the arrow's direction, and a green arrow that allows a left turn also allows a U-turn unless a road sign or marking forbids it.
ge-green-arrow-u-turn.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-lit-to-dark-eyes.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 25(10)(ა),(ბ),(გ): when driving from a lit stretch of road onto a dark one, the eyes adapt to the dark slowly, so an obstacle ahead is hard to notice; on poorly or unevenly lit roads at night road users see each other with difficulty, and in poor visibility the driver must slow down and increase the gap.
ge-lit-to-dark-eyes.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-railway-crossing-distances.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 39(3) and Art. 37(7)(ბ): when a level crossing is closed, stop at the stop line, sign 2.4 or the light, otherwise at least 5 m from the barrier, and if there is no barrier at least 10 m from the nearest rail; parking on the carriageway closer than 50 m to a level crossing is banned.
ge-railway-crossing-distances.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-inspection-retest-30-days.fact: Georgia, Government Resolution No. 191 of 22 May 2023 (amending the periodic technical inspection regulation, Resolution No. 510; in force 3 June 2023): after defects are found at a periodic inspection, the vehicle must be presented for re-inspection within 30 calendar days; if that is missed, a new periodic technical inspection must be carried out instead.
ge-inspection-retest-30-days.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), read 2026-10-12. Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. The consolidated regulation is behind a paywall, so later changes should be rechecked.

ge-inspection-minor-becomes-major.fact: Georgia, Government Resolution No. 191 of 22 May 2023 (amending Resolution No. 510): a vehicle with no defects or only minor ones passes, and minor defects are written in the report's remarks column; a minor defect noted there that is not fixed before the next periodic inspection is then treated as a major defect, and a major or dangerous defect means the inspection is not passed.
ge-inspection-minor-becomes-major.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), read 2026-10-12. Official texts are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-fine-no-inspection.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 118: driving a car that has not passed periodic technical inspection costs a private person 50 GEL; doing it again once 30 days have passed since that fine costs 150 GEL, then 300 GEL, then 500 GEL each further time, and no new fine for it can be given within 30 days of the last one.
ge-fine-no-inspection.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-inspection-exemptions.fact: Georgia's Ministry of Economy inspection page: periodic technical inspection does not apply to vehicles not registered under Georgian law, O1 and O2 trailers (750 to 3,500 kg), L-category (motorcycle-type) vehicles, historic vehicles made before 1960 whose type is out of production, historically protected and kept in original condition, vehicles taken out of use, and vehicles with a design speed of no more than 25 km/h.
ge-inspection-exemptions.licence_note: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia, official page, read 2026-10-12. Only the facts are used, restated in our own words.

ge-inspection-after-reregistration.fact: Georgia's Ministry of Economy inspection page: when a vehicle covered by the inspection schedule is re-registered, its periodic technical inspection must be carried out within 30 calendar days of that registration.
ge-inspection-after-reregistration.licence_note: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia, official page, read 2026-10-12. Only the facts are used, restated in our own words.

ge-licence-valid-15-years.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 58(2)(ბ),(გ): a licence for categories AM, A, B, BE, T and S (and subcategories A1, A2, B1) is valid for 15 years, or for a shorter period of up to 5 years if a medical certificate recommends a limited term; a licence for C, CE, D and DE (and C1, C1E, D1, D1E) is valid for 5 years, or up to 3 with such a medical recommendation.
ge-licence-valid-15-years.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-fine-drift.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(17),(18): deliberately skidding or drifting a vehicle, including spinning in circles, outside a professional sports event held under the law, costs 300 GEL; if it causes light damage to property or light injury, 500 GEL plus a 6-month driving suspension.
ge-fine-drift.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-fine-pedestrian-priority.fact: Georgia's Administrative Offences Code, Art. 125(5¹),(5²),(9¹) and note 8: breaking the traffic-law rules on conduct towards pedestrians costs 40 GEL, 150 GEL if repeated within a year, and 200 GEL if it creates an emergency, which includes a sharp manoeuvre on a pedestrian crossing, or braking hard, moving off or reversing while the pedestrian light is green.
ge-fine-pedestrian-priority.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words. Fines change: recheck before each film.

ge-lane-change-right-priority.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 32(4): when moving to another lane without changing direction, a driver must give way to vehicles already moving in that lane; if two vehicles change lanes at the same time and their paths cross, the vehicle on the right has priority.
ge-lane-change-right-priority.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.

ge-bus-stopped-at-crossing.fact: Georgian Law on Road Traffic, Art. 25(9): if a route bus or minibus stops or slows down before an unregulated pedestrian crossing, drivers in the neighbouring lanes may continue only after making sure there is no pedestrian in front of it.
ge-bus-stopped-at-crossing.licence_note: Official legal act of Georgia on matsne.gov.ge (the Legislative Herald), consolidated version read 2026-10-12. Official texts of laws are not protected by copyright under Georgian copyright law; restated in our own words.
